assertions.source: q^6-q^5+2q^4-2q^3+2q^2-2q+1 equals q^5*J(6_2) identically. The Jones polynomial being compared against survives in the ratio's DENOMINATOR.

assertions.name: q_plus_1_exponent_equals_n_minus_1
assertions.source: the other denominator factor is (q+1)^5 at 6 strands -- the exponent the omitted normalisation carries, so it is accounted for and is not evidence against the identification.

assertions.name: J62_numerator_does_NOT_divide_the_trace
assertions.source: THE RESULT. Polynomial division after q -> t^2 leaves a nonzero remainder, so no rescaling makes the trace a multiple of J(6_2).

assertions.name: J62_numerator_irreducible_and_coprime_to_the_normalisation_factors
assertions.source: irreducible over Q, gcd 1 with both (q-1) and (q+1). This is what makes the divisibility failure CONVENTION-INDEPENDENT: no monomial*(1+/-q)^k normalisation can contribute the missing factor.

description: EXPLORATORY. qou-5vhf hands over the target 'aim at the ratio being a pure power of -q^{1/2}', taken from atom_nf_symbolic_D.py:290. That test is MISCALIBRATED: the same file's docstring (line 194) names the omitted factor as ((-1/sqrt q)^{n-1} * (q/(1-q^2))^{n-1}), a RATIONAL function, so a non-monomial ratio is what a CORRECT identification would give. Factoring the committed ratio shows the denominator is 32*q^1327*(q+1)^5*(q^5*J(6_2)): the (q+1)^5 carries exponent n-1=5 and is accounted for by the missing normalisation, while the degree-6 factor is EXACTLY the numerator of J(6_2), surviving in the denominator. The gate STANDS on a sharper test -- q^5*J(6_2) does not divide the trace (remainder 12 terms), and being irreducible over Q and coprime to (q-1) and (q+1) it cannot be supplied by any normalisation of the shape monomial*(1+/-q)^k. Convention-independent, unlike the stated test. Scope (a) on the EVIDENCE, not on the knot. Nothing wired.

the_contradiction_inside_one_file.line_290_comment: the ratio should be a pure power of -q^{1/2}
the_contradiction_inside_one_file.why_incompatible: (q/(1-q^2))^{n-1} is a rational function with a (1-q^2)^{n-1} denominator; a pure power of -q^{1/2} is a monomial. If the docstring names the omitted factor, a non-monomial ratio is what a CORRECT identification gives, and the stated test cannot discriminate.
the_contradiction_inside_one_file.consequence_for_the_handover: qou-5vhf's closing recommendation points the next agent at the miscalibrated target; this probe replaces it with the divisibility test.

ratio_structure.reading: (q+1)^5 carries exponent n-1 at 6 strands, matching the exponent of the docstring's omitted factor, so it is accounted for. Matching an exponent is NOT verifying the convention and no such claim is made here.

the_sharp_test.conclusion: J(6_2)'s numerator is irreducible and coprime to (q-1) and (q+1), so no normalisation of the shape monomial*(1+/-q)^k -- the shape every Markov-to-Jones convention takes -- can supply it. Hence tr != N*J(6_2) for every such N. The gate stands, convention-independently.
